memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "With the bull offer a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with oil; with the ram, two-tenths; and with each of the seven lambs, one-tenth. Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you. These are in addition to the monthly and daily burnt offerings with their grain offerings and drink offerings as specified. They are food offerings presented to the LORD, a pleasing aroma." - Num 29:3-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The offerings for this feast day were brought "in addition to" the monthly and daily offerings. Worship was layered upon worship. The special did not cancel the regular; the daily rhythm continued even as the festival was celebrated. God's people were surrounded by opportunities to draw near to Him at every level of time.

Notice again the presence of the sin offering, a goat to make atonement, even on this joyful day of trumpets. No gathering before God was complete without acknowledging the need for cleansing. Joy and the confession of sin belonged together. The people rejoiced, yet never presumed to come before God without atonement.

We remember that these ceremonial forms were shadows fulfilled in Christ; we do not bring goats and bulls today. But the pattern teaches us that worship is meant to be woven richly through our lives, and that we always come to God through the provision He makes for our sin. We do not approach on our own merit.

The wonderful news is that the atonement Israel sought repeatedly has been made once for all in Christ. His one sacrifice covers us completely, so that every time we draw near, we come cleansed by His blood (Heb 10:14). Layer your life with worship, and rejoice that you come to God not through repeated sacrifices but through the finished work of Jesus.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is worship woven richly through your life, or only occasional?
2. Why is it important to come to God through His provision for sin?
3. How does Christ's once-for-all atonement change the way you approach God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, weave worship through every part of my life. Thank You that I come to You not on my own merit but cleansed by the once-for-all sacrifice of Christ. Draw me near with a grateful heart. Amen.
